items.name: First name
items.description: The new employee's first name, used to register the employee at the pension fund and by HR for its records and correspondence.
items.asked_when: Always (step 1 'About you').

needed_by.purpose: Required field 'First name' for the registration.
Identify the employee and address documents.

items.name: Last name
items.description: The new employee's last name.
items.asked_when: Always (step 1 'About you').

needed_by.purpose: Required field 'Last name' for the registration.
Identify the employee and address documents.

items.name: Date of birth
items.description: The new employee's date of birth. Assumption (D-050): the employee must be at least 14 and at most 100 years old on the first working day.
items.form: Date in the format DD.MM.YYYY. Employee at least 14 and at most 100 years old on the first working day.
items.asked_when: Always (step 1 'About you').

needed_by.purpose: Required field 'Date of birth' for the registration.

items.name: First working day
items.description: The contractual start date of employment, even when it falls on a weekend or public holiday (assumption D-039). The employee enters/confirms it because it often moves. After submission only HR can change it; the latest date always counts and no history of earlier dates is kept. The insurance start date and the reference date for children's age and for the address are derived from it.
items.form: Date in the format DD.MM.YYYY. Must lie within one year after the questionnaire is sent.
items.asked_when: Always (step 1 'About you').

needed_by.purpose: Basis for the insurance start date.
Plans the start and keeps the fund registration up to date when the date moves.

items.name: Street
items.description: Street of the employee's home address as it applies on the first working day (assumption D-041).
items.form: Part of a normal postal address as written on an envelope: street, house number, postcode, town and country.
items.asked_when: Always (step 2 'Home address').

needed_by.purpose: HR posts many documents to employees; the address must be complete.

items.name: House number
items.description: House number of the home address as it applies on the first working day. Required; an explicit 'no house number' option covers addresses without one (assumption D-042).
items.form: Part of a normal postal address: street, house number, postcode, town and country. Explicit 'no house number' option.
items.asked_when: Always (step 2 'Home address').
items.required_when: Always (a house number or the explicit 'no house number' option).

needed_by.purpose: Complete postal address for documents.

items.name: Postcode
items.description: Postcode of the home address as it applies on the first working day.
items.form: Part of a normal postal address: street, house number, postcode, town and country.
items.asked_when: Always (step 2 'Home address').

needed_by.purpose: Complete postal address for documents.

items.name: Town
items.description: Town of the home address as it applies on the first working day.
items.form: Part of a normal postal address: street, house number, postcode, town and country.
items.asked_when: Always (step 2 'Home address').

needed_by.purpose: Complete postal address for documents.

items.name: Country of residence (country of the home address)
items.description: Country of the home address as it applies on the first working day; this is the employee's country of residence. Decides whether the employee lives in Switzerland or abroad (source tax liability, which further questions apply, the canton for the pension fund, the cross-border questions and the permit reminder).
items.form: Country chosen from the ISO 3166 country list, by English name (e.g. Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein).
items.asked_when: Always (step 2 'Home address').

needed_by.purpose: Complete postal address for documents.
Employees living abroad are always subject to source tax; residence country drives the cross-border tariff questions.
Decides whether the canton is chosen by the employee or set to the canton of the place of work.

items.name: Canton of residence
items.description: The Swiss canton the employee lives in on the first working day, for the pension fund's 'Canton' field. Only asked of employees living in Switzerland; for employees abroad the canton of the place of work (Zurich) is entered instead and not asked (assumption D-002).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Switzerland (step 2 'Home address').

needed_by.purpose: Required field 'Canton' for the registration.

items.name: Nationality
items.description: The employee's nationality, to decide source tax liability for employees living in Switzerland. Anyone holding Swiss citizenship (also together with another nationality) answers Switzerland and counts as Swiss (D-008). Not asked of employees living abroad, who are subject to source tax whatever their nationality (data minimisation).
items.form: Country chosen from the ISO 3166 country list, plus 'stateless'.
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Switzerland (step 3 'Nationality and C permit').

needed_by.purpose: Swiss employees living in Switzerland are not subject to source tax.
Decides whether the permit reminder is shown.

items.name: Holds a C permit
items.description: Whether a non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland holds a C permit (permanent residence). C-permit holders are treated like Swiss people for source tax. No other permit type is asked (D-005).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Switzerland and is not Swiss (step 3).

needed_by.purpose: A C permit exempts the employee from source tax.

items.name: Civil status
items.description: The employee's civil status. Used for the pension fund (Registered partnership and Separated are entered there as Married, assumption D-003) and for source tax (Registered partnership counts as married, Separated as single, as in the calculator). Asked of everyone, wherever they live.
items.asked_when: Always (step 4 'Civil status and spouse').

needed_by.purpose: Required field 'Civil status'.
Determines the tariff group and the spouse exemption.

items.name: Spouse's / registered partner's date of birth
items.description: Date of birth of the spouse or registered partner. Asked of married employees, registered partners and separated employees (all entered at the fund as Married); not of divorced or widowed employees (assumption D-004).
items.asked_when: Only if civil status is Married, Registered partnership or Separated (step 4).

needed_by.purpose: Required when civil status is Married; registration is blocked without it.

items.name: Spouse's nationality
items.description: Nationality of the spouse or registered partner, to check the spouse exemption from source tax (married to a Swiss national who lives in Switzerland). Only needed when the employee would otherwise be subject to source tax.
items.form: Country chosen from the ISO 3166 country list, plus 'stateless'.
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss, has no C permit and is married or in a registered partnership (step 4).
items.asked_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"]
items.required_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"]

needed_by.purpose: Spouse exemption from source tax.

items.name: Spouse holds a C permit
items.description: Whether a non-Swiss spouse or registered partner holds a C permit, for the spouse exemption from source tax. No other permit type is asked (D-005).
items.asked_when: Only if the spouse question applies (see spouse's nationality) and the spouse is not Swiss (step 4).
items.asked_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and spouse_nationality != "Switzerland"
items.required_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and spouse_nationality != "Switzerland"

needed_by.purpose: Spouse exemption from source tax.

items.name: Spouse lives in Switzerland
items.description: Whether the spouse or registered partner lives in Switzerland, asked as 'Does your spouse live in Switzerland? yes/no' (D-050). Only relevant when the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit.
items.asked_when: Only if the spouse question applies and the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit (step 4).
items.asked_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_holds_c_permit == "yes")
items.required_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_holds_c_permit == "yes")

needed_by.purpose: Spouse exemption applies only if the spouse lives in Switzerland.

items.name: Daily return to Liechtenstein
items.description: Whether the employee living in Liechtenstein expects to return daily to the main residence in Liechtenstein. Asked before denomination, spouse and children questions (D-040).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Liechtenstein (step 5 'Cross-border commuting').

needed_by.purpose: Decides whether there is in principle no source tax liability.

items.name: More than 45 work-related non-return days (Liechtenstein)
items.description: Whether the employee living in Liechtenstein who does not return daily expects more than 45 work-related non-return days in the calendar year (a declaration of expectation, D-035).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Liechtenstein and does not return daily (step 5).

needed_by.purpose: More than 45 days gives the normal tariff subject to the double taxation agreement.

items.name: Daily return to Germany
items.description: Whether the employee living in Germany expects to return daily to the main residence in Germany.
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Germany (step 5).

needed_by.purpose: Decides the cross-border tariff.

items.name: Certificate of residence handed in
items.description: Whether the employee living in Germany who returns daily has a certificate of residence for HR. 'Not yet' is a valid answer and counts as 'no' for the tariff code. The document itself goes to HR outside Lonio; there is no upload (D-035).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Germany and returns daily (step 5).

needed_by.purpose: With a certificate the cross-border tariff applies.
Knows that a certificate is still expected.

items.name: Daily return reasonable (less than 100 km)
items.description: Whether, for an employee living in Germany who does not return daily, a daily return would basically be reasonable (less than 100 km driving distance).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Germany and does not return daily (step 5).

needed_by.purpose: Decides the cross-border tariff.

items.name: More than 60 work-related non-return days (Germany)
items.description: Whether the employee living in Germany, for whom daily return is reasonable, expects more than 60 work-related non-return days in the calendar year (a declaration of expectation, not proof, D-035).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Germany, does not return daily and daily return is reasonable (step 5).

needed_by.purpose: More than 60 days gives the normal tariff; otherwise the cross-border tariff.

items.name: Denomination
items.description: The employee's religious denomination, which sets the church-tax suffix of the tariff code (Y or N).
allowed_values: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed
items.asked_when: Only if the employee is subject to source tax and, for Liechtenstein residents, has more than 45 non-return days (step 6 'Source tax details').

needed_by.purpose: Church-tax suffix of the tariff code.

items.name: Spouse gainfully employed
items.description: Whether the spouse or registered partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income. Decides tariff C (yes) or B (no).
items.asked_when: Only if the source tax details apply (see denomination) and the employee is married or in a registered partnership (step 6).
items.asked_when_expr: subject_to_source_tax and (address_country != "Liechtenstein" or non_return_days_45 == "yes") and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"]
items.required_when_expr: subject_to_source_tax and (address_country != "Liechtenstein" or non_return_days_45 == "yes") and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"]

needed_by.purpose: Tariff letter B or C.

items.name: Has biological or adopted children
items.description: Whether the employee (for married employees and registered partners: the employee or the spouse/partner) has biological or adopted children.
items.asked_when: Only if the source tax details apply (step 6).

needed_by.purpose: Opens the child questions that determine the child digit.

items.name: Child: minor or adult in first education
items.description: Per child (one block per child, no maximum number, D-044): whether the child is a minor, an adult in first education, or neither, judged on the first working day (assumption D-044). 'Neither' ends the child block; the child does not count.
items.asked_when: For each child, if the employee has children (step 7 'Children').

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result and child digit.

items.name: Child lives in the same household
items.description: Per child: whether the child lives in the employee's household.
items.asked_when: For each child who is a minor or an adult in first education.
items.asked_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_age_status in ["Minor", "Adult and in first education"]
items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_age_status in ["Minor", "Adult and in first education"]

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result.

items.name: Child: parental custody
items.description: Per minor child living in the household: whether parental custody is shared or sole.
items.asked_when: For each minor child living in the same household.

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result.

items.name: Child: common household with the other parent
items.description: Per child: whether the employee lives in a common household with the child's other parent.
items.asked_when: For a minor child in the household with shared custody, or an adult child in first education living in the household.
items.asked_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_same_household == "yes" and ((child_age_status == "Minor" and child_custody == "Shared custody") or child_age_status == "Adult and in first education")
items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_same_household == "yes" and ((child_age_status == "Minor" and child_custody == "Shared custody") or child_age_status == "Adult and in first education")

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result.

items.name: Child: shared custody (child not in household, married)
items.description: Per minor child not living in the household of a married employee or registered partner: whether custody is shared.
items.asked_when: For a minor child not in the household, if the employee is married or in a registered partnership.
items.asked_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"
items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result.

items.name: Child: parental care (child not in household, not married)
items.description: Per minor child not living in the household of an employee who is single, divorced, widowed or separated: whether the employee has parental care.
items.asked_when: For a minor child not in the household, if the employee is single, divorced, widowed or separated.
items.asked_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"
items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result.

items.name: Child: alternating custody
items.description: Per minor child: whether there is alternating custody with the other parent.
items.asked_when: For a minor child: in the household with shared custody and no common household with the other parent; or not in the household with shared custody (married) or parental care (not married).
items.asked_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_age_status == "Minor" and ((child_same_household == "yes" and child_custody == "Shared custody" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no") or child_shared_custody == "yes" or child_parental_care == "yes")
items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_age_status == "Minor" and ((child_same_household == "yes" and child_custody == "Shared custody" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no") or child_shared_custody == "yes" or child_parental_care == "yes")

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result.

items.name: Child: larger financial contributor
items.description: Per child: who makes the larger financial contribution to the child's maintenance - the employee or the other parent.
items.asked_when: For a child with alternating custody, or - for employees who are single, divorced, widowed or separated - a child in the household where the employee lives with the other parent.
items.asked_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and (child_alternating_custody == "yes" or (civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "yes"))
items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and (child_alternating_custody == "yes" or (civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "yes"))

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result (H tariff for single parents).

items.name: Child: more than 50% of maintenance provided
items.description: Per adult child in first education: whether the employee mainly (more than 50%) provides for the child's maintenance.
items.asked_when: For an adult child in first education who is not in the household, or is in the household without a common household with the other parent.
items.asked_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_age_status == "Adult and in first education" and (child_same_household == "no" or child_common_household_other_parent == "no")
items.required_when_expr: has_children == "yes" and child_age_status == "Adult and in first education" and (child_same_household == "no" or child_common_household_other_parent == "no")

needed_by.purpose: Per-child result.

rules.name: Questionnaire flow
rules.statement: The questionnaire has exactly eight steps in this order (assumption D-047). Each question appears only when at least one receiving party needs the answer for this person. Answers are saved as the employee goes; the employee can resume until submitting; going back and changing an earlier answer keeps the other answers until submission; submitting needs one confirmation on a summary page (D-050). For Liechtenstein residents the cross-border questions come before the source tax details, which are skipped when there is in principle no source tax liability (D-040).

table.then: First name, last name, date of birth, first working day - asked of everyone.
Street, house number (or 'no house number'), postcode, town, country as on the first working day - everyone; canton only if living in Switzerland.
Only employees living in Switzerland: nationality; C permit (yes/no) only if not Swiss.
Civil status for everyone; spouse's date of birth if Married, Registered partnership or Separated; spouse's nationality, C permit and residence in Switzerland only for spouse exemption check.
Only residents of Liechtenstein or Germany (all subject to source tax): the daily-return and non-return-day questions, and for Germany the certificate of residence.
Only employees subject to source tax (and not exempt in principle as Liechtenstein residents): denomination, spouse gainfully employed (married/registered partners), has children.
Only if the employee has children: one block per child with the child questions.
Permit reminder (non-Swiss or living abroad), summary page, one confirmation to submit.

rules.name: Insurance start date
rules.statement: The pension fund insurance start date is derived from the first working day (the contractual start date, assumption D-039), never asked: if the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise on the 1st of the following month (e.g. 15.03.2026 gives 01.04.2026). It is always derived again from the latest first working day.
inputs: First working day is the 1st of a month

table.then: Insurance starts on the first working day.
Insurance starts on the 1st of the following month.

rules.name: Civil status for the pension fund
rules.statement: The fund only accepts Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed. Registered partnership and Separated are entered as Married (with the partner's/spouse's date of birth); the others unchanged (assumption D-003).

rules.name: Canton for the pension fund
rules.statement: Employees living in Switzerland: the canton they chose. Employees living abroad: the canton of the place of work, Zurich for Muster AG, not asked (assumption D-002).

rules.name: Subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee living abroad is subject to source tax whatever their nationality. An employee living in Switzerland is subject only if not Swiss (Swiss citizenship, also as dual nationality, counts as Swiss), without a C permit, and not married or in a registered partnership with a Swiss national or C-permit holder who lives in Switzerland. Separated counts as single, so no spouse exemption. ('Here' in HR's wording means Switzerland; assumption D-043.) Always derived again from the latest answers.
rules.expression: address_country != null and (address_country != "Switzerland" or (nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and not (civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_holds_c_permit == "yes") and spouse_residence_country == "yes")))

rules.name: Liechtenstein: in principle no source tax liability
rules.statement: Liechtenstein residents are asked the source tax questions (HR's rule). With daily return, or without daily return and at most 45 non-return days, the result is 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead of a tariff code, flagged for HR, and the remaining tariff questions are skipped. With more than 45 non-return days the normal tariff code applies with the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR (assumption D-040).

table.then: In principle no source tax liability
In principle no source tax liability
Normal tariff code, subject to the double taxation agreement

rules.name: Civil status for source tax
rules.statement: Married and Registered partnership count as 'married or registered partnership'; Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated count as 'single, divorced, separated or widowed', as in the calculator.
rules.expression: if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "Married or registered partnership", if_else(civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"], "Single, divorced, separated or widowed", null))

rules.name: Residence for source tax
rules.statement: The country of residence is grouped as in the calculator: Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein or other country. Switzerland and other country lead to the base tariff without further residence questions.
rules.expression: if_else(address_country == "Switzerland", "Switzerland", if_else(address_country == "Germany", "Germany", if_else(address_country == "Liechtenstein", "Liechtenstein", if_else(address_country != null, "Other country", null))))

rules.name: Church-tax suffix
rules.statement: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed gives suffix Y; none or other gives N.

when: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

rules.expression: if_else(confession == "Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed", "Y", if_else(confession == "None or other", "N", null))

rules.name: Per-child source tax result
rules.statement: For each child, the answers give one of: counted, counted with H (single parents), or not counted - following the calculator. Observed calculator rows win over the derived logic (assumption D-046); rows marked inferred are not observed and are checked before go-live (D-009).
rules.expression: if_else(child_age_status == "Neither", "not counted", if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", if_else(child_age_status == "Minor", if_else(child_same_household == "yes", if_else(child_custody == "Sole custody" or child_common_household_other_parent == "yes" or (child_alternating_custody == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "Me"), "counted", "not counted"), if_else(child_shared_custody == "yes" and child_alternating_custody == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "Me", "counted", "not counted")), if_else(child_common_household_other_parent == "yes" or child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes", "counted", "not counted")), if_else(child_age_status == "Minor", if_else(child_same_household == "yes", if_else(child_custody == "Sole custody" or child_main_financial_contributor == "Me" or (child_common_household_other_parent == "no" and child_alternating_custody == "no"), "counted with H", "not counted"), if_else(child_parental_care == "yes" and child_alternating_custody == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "Me", "counted with H", "not counted")), if_else(child_same_household == "yes", if_else(child_main_financial_contributor == "Me" or child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes", "counted with H", "not counted"), if_else(child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes", "counted", "not counted")))))

rules.name: Child digit of the tariff code
rules.statement: The child digit equals the number of children whose per-child result is 'counted' or 'counted with H' (e.g. three counted children give C3Y). Without children the digit is 0. (The expression gives, per child, whether that child is counted; the digit is the number of children for which it is true.)

rules.name: Base tariff letter
rules.statement: Married/registered partners: C if the spouse is gainfully employed, otherwise B. Single, divorced, separated or widowed: H if at least one child is counted with H, otherwise A.
inputs: At least one child counted with H
rules.expression: if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", if_else(spouse_gainful_employment == "yes", "C", "B"), if_else(child_result == "counted with H", "H", "A"))

rules.name: Cross-border tariff applies (Germany)
rules.statement: For Germany residents the cross-border tariff applies with daily return and a certificate of residence ('not yet' counts as no), or without daily return when daily return is reasonable and the employee does not expect more than 60 non-return days. Otherwise the normal tariff applies. Other countries never get the cross-border tariff.
rules.expression: address_country == "Germany" and ((daily_return_germany == "yes" and residence_certificate == "yes") or (daily_return_germany == "no" and daily_return_reasonable == "yes" and non_return_days_60 == "no"))

rules.name: Tariff letter
rules.statement: Without the cross-border tariff the base letter applies. With it: A becomes L, B becomes M, C becomes N, H becomes P (and G would become Q, as the calculator shows; G does not occur because replacement income is out of scope, D-006).
rules.expression: if_else(cross_border_tariff, if_else(base_tariff_letter == "A", "L", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "B", "M", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "C", "N", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "H", "P", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "G", "Q", null))))), base_tariff_letter)

rules.name: Source tax tariff code
rules.statement: Lonio computes the full Zurich tariff code for every employee subject to source tax, replacing HR's manual calculator step: one text made of tariff letter, child digit and church-tax suffix, e.g. 'C1Y', 'L0Y', 'N1Y'. Employees not subject to source tax get 'no tariff code'. Liechtenstein residents with in principle no liability get 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR; with more than 45 non-return days the code carries the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR. If HR later changes an answer so that unanswered questions apply, the result is 'incomplete - HR must complete' until HR enters them (assumption D-048). Always derived again from the latest answers. Computed codes are not legally binding, like the calculator's.
inputs: In principle no source tax liability

table.then: 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR
Full tariff code with note 'subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR
Full tariff code (letter + child digit + church-tax suffix)

rules.expression: if_else(not subject_to_source_tax, "no tariff code", if_else(liechtenstein_no_source_tax, "in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement", tariff_letter + child_count + church_tax_suffix))

rules.name: Permit reminder
rules.statement: At the end of the questionnaire, every non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland and every employee living abroad (whatever their nationality, which is not asked of them) is reminded to bring their permit on the first working day. HR provides the wording before go-live, worded so that a Swiss citizen living abroad sees it does not apply to them. It collects no data.

rules.name: Discard answers that no longer apply
rules.statement: Answers to questions that no longer apply after an earlier answer changes are kept while the employee goes back and forth, and discarded on submission. The same applies when HR changes an answer after submission (D-048).

rules.name: Read-only after submission
rules.statement: After submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee. Later changes (a move, marriage, new child, a certificate of residence handed in later, a corrected nationality, a moved first working day) are made by HR (specified later).
